name: Ruy Lopez
summary: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5: the bishop attacks the knight that defends e5. The pressure is slow but it lasts the whole game. White builds with Re1, c3, h3 and d4; Black spends time on ...a6 and ...b5 to chase the bishop.

white: Pressure e5 through the c6 knight: Bb5, then Re1 and d4.
Prepare d4 with c3, and play h3 first so ...Bg4 cannot pin the f3 knight.
Keep the light-squared bishop: Ba4, Bb3, and Bc2 when ...Na5 hits it.
In the closed lines, re-route the queen's knight: Nbd2, Nf1, Ng3.
black: Ask the bishop at once with ...a6: it must trade or retreat.
Gain queenside space with ...b5 and develop with ...Be7 and ...O-O.
In the Open Spanish, take on e4 and hold the knight there with ...b5 and ...d5.
Counter on the queenside: ...Na5, ...c5 and ...Qc7 in the Chigorin.

structures.name: Closed Spanish: e4 and d4 against e5 and d6
structures.text: A tense centre that White keeps with c3 and h3. White re-routes the queen's knight to g3 and plays on the kingside; Black plays ...Na5, ...c5 and gains space on the queenside.

structures.name: Exchange Spanish: doubled c-pawns for Black
structures.text: After Bxc6 dxc6 Black has the bishop pair, White a healthy kingside majority, four pawns against three. White wants an endgame where that majority makes a passed pawn; Black wants open lines for the two bishops.

structures.name: Berlin endgame
structures.text: Queens come off at move eight. Black's king stays in the centre, but without queens nobody can attack it. White has a kingside pawn majority; Black has the bishop pair and a sound structure.

white: Spanish bishop on b5, a4 or b3: long-term pressure on e5 and later on f7.
e1 rook: makes e5 a real target and guards e4.
f3 knight: holds d4 and e5; protect it from the ...Bg4 pin with h3.
Queen's knight: d2, f1, g3 when the centre is closed.
black: c6 knight: the target. It often goes to a5 to hit the bishop and support ...c5.
e7 bishop: modest but solid; it guards the king and the centre pawns.
f6 knight: hits e4 and keeps the kingside safe.
Light-squared bishop: b7 after ...b5, or e6 in the Open Spanish.

lines.name: Closed Spanish, Chigorin: the main road
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Ba4 Nf6 5. O-O Be7 6. Re1 b5 7. Bb3 d6 8. c3 O-O 9. h3 Na5 10. Bc2 c5 11. d4 Qc7 12. Nbd2

notes.3.Bb5: Attacks the c6 knight, the defender of e5. It is not a threat yet: Bxc6 and Nxe5 would be met by ...Qd4, hitting the knight and e4.
notes.3...a6: Asks the bishop to decide: trade on c6 or retreat.
notes.5.O-O: Castles although e4 is attacked: after ...Nxe4 White wins the pawn back with Re1 or d4.
notes.5...Be7: The closed system: Black develops and castles before anything else.
notes.6.Re1: Defends e4. Now Bxc6 and Nxe5 is a real threat.
notes.6...b5: Ends the threat by chasing the bishop.
notes.7.Bb3: From b3 the bishop aims at f7.
notes.8.c3: Prepares d4 and gives the bishop the c2 square.
notes.9.h3: Stops ...Bg4, which would pin the knight that defends d4.
notes.9...Na5: Chigorin's idea: hit the bishop and free the c-pawn.
notes.10.Bc2: The bishop keeps its diagonal towards the kingside.
notes.10...c5: Space on the queenside and pressure on d4.
notes.11...Qc7: Supports e5 and lines up on the c-file.
notes.12.Nbd2: The knight heads for f1 and g3.

lines.name: Open Spanish: why the knight can take e4
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Ba4 Nf6 5. O-O Nxe4 6. d4 b5 7. Bb3 d5 8. dxe5 Be6 9. c3 Bc5 10. Nbd2 O-O 11. Bc2

notes.5...Nxe4: Black takes the pawn. It is not a blunder: White wins it back, but Black gets free piece play.
notes.6.d4: Opens the centre while Black's king is still on e8.
notes.6...b5: Chases the bishop away from c6 before the centre opens.
notes.7...d5: Holds the e4 knight with a pawn.
notes.9.c3: Keeps a retreat for the bishop on c2.
notes.9...Bc5: The most active square for the bishop.
notes.11.Bc2: The bishop joins the attack on e4.

lines.name: Berlin Defence: the endgame at move eight
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nf6 4. O-O Nxe4 5. d4 Nd6 6. Bxc6 dxc6 7. dxe5 Nf5 8. Qxd8+ Kxd8 9. Nc3 Ke8 10. h3 h5

notes.3...Nf6: Black counterattacks e4 instead of asking the bishop with ...a6.
notes.4.O-O: e4 can be given: White wins it back.
notes.5...Nd6: The knight retreats with an attack on the bishop.
notes.6.Bxc6: Trades before the bishop is chased.
notes.7.dxe5: White gains space; the knight must move.
notes.8.Qxd8+: Queens off. Black has lost the right to castle, but without queens the king is safe.
notes.9...Ke8: Back to e8, so the rooks can connect later.
notes.10.h3: Prepares g4 to chase the f5 knight.
notes.10...h5: Stops g4 and gives the h8 rook a road via h6.

lines.name: Exchange Variation: play for the endgame
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Bxc6 dxc6 5. O-O f6 6. d4 exd4 7. Nxd4 c5 8. Nb3 Qxd1 9. Rxd1 Bg4 10. f3 Be6

notes.4.Bxc6: White gives the bishop pair to damage Black's pawns.
notes.4...dxc6: Takes towards the centre and opens lines for both bishops.
notes.5.O-O: Castles and renews the idea of Nxe5.
notes.5...f6: Defends e5 with a pawn and keeps the queen free.
notes.6.d4: Opens the centre to reach the endgame.
notes.8...Qxd1: Queens off: White's four against three on the kingside is the long-term trump.
notes.9...Bg4: Develops with an attack on the rook.
notes.10.f3: Blunts the bishop; the pawn supports e4 and a later kingside advance.
notes.10...Be6: Eyes c4 and the b3 knight.

lines.name: Marshall Attack: what 8...d5 offers
lines.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Ba4 Nf6 5. O-O Be7 6. Re1 b5 7. Bb3 O-O 8. c3 d5 9. exd5 Nxd5 10. Nxe5 Nxe5 11. Rxe5 c6 12. d4 Bd6 13. Re1 Qh4 14. g3 Qh3

notes.7...O-O: Castling before ...d6 keeps the option of ...d5.
notes.8...d5: Marshall's pawn sacrifice: Black opens lines towards White's king.
notes.10.Nxe5: White accepts: a pawn is a pawn.
notes.11...c6: Supports the d5 knight and prepares ...Bd6.
notes.12.d4: Opens the c1 bishop's diagonal so it can come to e3 and defend.
notes.14.g3: Blocks the queen's attack on h2.
notes.14...Qh3: The queen sits next to the king. White defends with Be3, Qd3 and Re4: a full pawn against a lasting attack.

traps.name: Noah's Ark: the bishop gets trapped
traps.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Ba4 d6 5. d4 b5 6. Bb3 Nxd4 7. Nxd4 exd4 8. Qxd4 c5 9. Qd5 Be6 10. Qc6+ Bd7 11. Qd5 c4

notes.4...d6: Black supports e5 and waits for the bishop.
notes.6...Nxd4: Sets the trap: Black trades on d4 to bring the white queen there.
notes.8.Qxd4: The mistake: the queen recaptures and walks into ...c5.

traps.punishment: 8...c5 hits the queen, and after 9.Qd5 Be6 10.Qc6+ Bd7 11.Qd5 c4 the bishop on b3 is caught behind a wall of pawns on a6, b5 and c4. White loses a piece. 8.a4, attacking the b5 pawn, keeps the bishop out of the ark.

traps.name: Tarrasch Trap: the e-file pin in the Open Spanish
traps.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4. Ba4 Nf6 5. O-O Nxe4 6. d4 b5 7. Bb3 d5 8. dxe5 Be6 9. c3 Be7 10. Re1 O-O 11. Nd4 Qd7 12. Nxe6 fxe6 13. Rxe4

notes.10.Re1: The rook lines up with the e4 knight.
notes.11.Nd4: Offers a trade on e6 that opens the f-file and the a2-g8 diagonal.
notes.11...Qd7: The mistake: the queen steps onto the diagonal of the b3 bishop.

traps.punishment: 12.Nxe6 fxe6 13.Rxe4 wins a piece: 13...dxe4 opens the diagonal and 14.Bxe6+ hits the king and the queen on d7 at once. Black should take the pawn with 11...Nxe5 instead.

traps.name: Fishing Pole: do not take the knight on g4
traps.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nf6 4. O-O Ng4 5. h3 h5 6. hxg4 hxg4 7. Ne1 Qh4 8. f3 g3

notes.4...Ng4: The bait: the knight sits where the h3 pawn can take it.
notes.5...h5: Black backs the knight with the h-pawn, so the h-file opens if White takes.
notes.6.hxg4: The mistake: White takes a whole piece and opens the h-file towards the king.

traps.punishment: 6...hxg4 hits the f3 knight and opens the h-file for the h8 rook. After 7.Ne1 Qh4 8.f3 g3 mate on h1 or h2 cannot be stopped. White should ignore the knight with 6.d3: the bait is a piece, the price is the king.
